 Older adults urged to seek help with their Medicare plan during the open enrollment period. (Spectrum News 1) 
 Older adults urged to seek professional guidance when reviewing Medicare Advantage plan
 BY 
 Mark Goshgarian 
 Buffalo 
 PUBLISHED 6:29 PM ET Oct. 20, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 6:29 PM EDT Oct. 20, 2026 
 SHARE 
 BUFFALO, N.Y. — Anna Diliberto, 77, is retired and on a fixed income, and is looking to review her existing Medicare Advantage healthcare plan for any upcoming coverage changes next year.
 "Definitely prescriptions, the wellness benefits. What the premium is going to be, out-of-pocket costs. All of that is important to me," said Anna.
 Too important for her to try and figure out on her own.
 "Extremely overwhelming, because there are so many plans, so many changes," said Anna.
 Which is why she's meeting with Independent Health to discuss her current plan and prescription drug coverage, known as Part D.
 Leaders say the challenge is knowing what each plan covers.
 "Navigating on your own can be pretty overwhelming and it can be daunting. It's your opportunity to really sit down and talk about yourself, and your needs," said Cathy Aquino, group vice president of sales, Medicare and consumer & small markets for Independent Health.
 Some insurers are shutting down or scaling back their plans, especially in rural areas, impacting close to half a million upstate New Yorkers.
 Rising medical and drug costs are surpassing reimbursement rates and funding from the federal government, forcing many companies like Independent Health to reduce the number of plans available, with minimal changes to the existing ones.
 "Some slight premium increases, maybe some deductible changes," said Cathy.
 Which is why Cathy tells older adults, like Anna, a plan that looks inexpensive may come with higher out of pocket expenses down the road when they need care.
 "But if you go with a slightly higher premium plan, then the reverse happens. When you go to use it, you're going to have lower out-of-pocket costs. So, again, you've got to weigh out the differences," said Cathy.
 While Anna's premium is projected to go up slightly, she says her plan is still very manageable, and urges others to review theirs to make sure it's tailor-fit for them.
 "This way they are well educated about the plan. Relief and peace of mind, peace of mind especially becasue these things can be very confusing and upsetting," said Anna.
 Because benefits and plans can change from year to year, experts say even older adults who are happy with their current coverage should still take time to review their options.
 Open enrollment closes Dec. 7, with changes taking effect Jan. 1. 
 Independent Health also recently announced the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services has released its Star Ratings for 2027.  
 Independent Health has again been recognized as a 4.5-star-rated Medicare plan by CMS for 2027, marking 17 consecutive years that Independent Health has achieved 4.5 or 5 Stars for its Medicare HMO plans and 12 consecutive years for its Medicare PPO plans.
